description_intent: The Windows authentication service LSASS accepts additional plug-in modules called Security Support Providers and Authentication Packages, and by default it will load ones that are not part of the operating system's own built-in set. This control closes that plug-in slot entirely, so LSASS only runs the authentication code it shipped with and nothing else can register itself into that pipeline.
rationale_intent: LSASS is the one process on a Windows endpoint that legitimately handles a user's raw credentials during every sign-in, which makes any code capable of running inside it a high-value target. A custom SSP or AP is, functionally, a way to get arbitrary code loaded into that trusted process and given a view into the authentication traffic passing through it - exactly the position credential-theft tooling wants to occupy. Closing off that loading mechanism means an attacker who compromises the endpoint still cannot use the SSP/AP interface as a route into LSASS's memory space, removing one of the more direct paths to bulk credential capture rather than merely making that path harder to notice.
